summary:
iteration_24 — Vitals lime-palette propagation across Design Hub / Compare / Community / Settings / Scenes. 5 of 6 review criteria PASS; #1 (grep sanity zero legacy hues) FAILS because the bulk sed missed several occurrences. Visual checks on /community (VERIFICADO badge is lime), /settings (both Feedback sensorial toggles ON = lime; Datos title = warm) and /scenes (empty state clean; code constants HUE_SYNC=#C9F03E, push=#F5B62E, share=#4A6BFF, HUE_DANGER=#FF6B4A) all match the intended palette. Compare page empty state renders CTA 'Ir a Escenas' with white bg as expected; the code constants A_HUE=#C9F03E and B_HUE=#F5B62E, plus DeltaStat 'hue' props at lines 297/304 (lime + amber), are correct. Vitest 78/78 GREEN and tsc -b --noEmit exits 0.

CRITICAL MISS — /app/src/pages/compare/index.tsx lines 720-721 in the DiffRow renderer (not the DeltaStat calls) still hardcodes the legacy sage #5BA777 and amethyst #9B7EBD for TrendingUp / TrendingDown icons. Since these render whenever two scenes are compared with acoustics diffs, the delta arrows will still visually use the OLD sage/amethyst hues even though A_HUE / B_HUE at the top of the file are lime/amber. Fix: swap #5BA777 → #C9F03E (or use A_HUE) and #9B7EBD → #F5B62E (or use B_HUE) on lines 720-721.

Additional grep hits (may be intentional audio-warning colors, but the review said 'zero occurrences with only 3 exceptions'): /app/src/components/soundmap/spl-meter.tsx:529 (#FF7A3A for '>90 dB' SumStat); /app/src/components/soundmap/spl-heatmap-2d.tsx lines 20/24/32/33/34 (#FF7A3A, #4EA8DE for SPL heatmap thresholds); /app/src/pages/kiosk/index.tsx:42 (#FF7A3A for 'hot' SPL band). These are semantic SPL warning-zone colors (audio-spec meaning: >102 dB, >78 dB, etc.), not UI accent tokens. Confirm with product whether they should also map to the new warm hue #FF6B4A or stay as-is for domain semantics. Kiosk was not called out in the review checklist.

ui_bugs.issue: Legacy hex #5BA777 (sage) and #9B7EBD (amethyst) hardcoded on TrendingUp / TrendingDown icons at lines 720-721. Violates the grep-sanity criterion and visually breaks A/B chromatic consistency (numbers use A_HUE=lime / B_HUE=amber correctly, but delta arrows still render sage/amethyst).
SumStat '>90 dB' still uses legacy #FF7A3A. If warm hue should follow the new #FF6B4A, replace here. Otherwise document as an intentional SPL-warning constant and exempt in the review checklist.
SPL heatmap threshold colors still use legacy #FF7A3A and #4EA8DE. Same call-out as spl-meter: either replace or explicitly exempt as SPL-band semantics.
bandColor('hot') still returns #FF7A3A. Kiosk not in review checklist but grep sanity says pages/*.tsx must return zero. Either propagate to #FF6B4A or exempt kiosk.

Regression: /, /design, /perform, /compare, /community, /settings all load without React ErrorBoundary; only /scenes loads as empty state (no seeded data); no page-crash console errors (only Vite HMR WSS + expected Cloudflare 429 retries). Vitest 78/78 pass in 6.44s. tsc -b --noEmit exits 0. ✅

action_items: HIGH: In /app/src/pages/compare/index.tsx L720-721, replace hardcoded 'text-[#5BA777]' → 'text-[#C9F03E]' (or reference A_HUE) and 'text-[#9B7EBD]' → 'text-[#F5B62E]' (or reference B_HUE) so DiffRow trend arrows match the new A_HUE/B_HUE lime+amber convention. This is the only miss that directly contradicts the review's chromatic-consistency intent.

MEDIUM: Decide on policy for SPL warning colors in spl-meter.tsx L529, spl-heatmap-2d.tsx L20-34, and kiosk/index.tsx L42. If they should follow the new palette, replace #FF7A3A → #FF6B4A and #4EA8DE → #4A6BFF. If they're intentional audio-spec constants, extend the review's exception list to cover them and adjust the grep-sanity criterion.

critical_code_review_comments: compare/index.tsx L720-721 — DiffRow uses the legacy sage/amethyst hardcoded via tailwind arbitrary values `text-[#5BA777]`/`text-[#9B7EBD]`. Because these are inside a template string with cn(...), grep still picks them up correctly, but they escaped the bulk sed that only targeted `#5BA777`/`#9B7EBD` as strings (or maybe was scoped to inline style props). Recommend a follow-up sed OR — better — replace with the file-level A_HUE / B_HUE constants so future palette changes are localized.
compare/index.tsx L286 — 'A más fuerte' chip uses `background: '#C9F03E'` inline. Fine and correct, but consider using the A_HUE constant here too for DRY.

spl-heatmap-2d.tsx — This file is a strong candidate for a dedicated 'SPL semantic palette' constant module: bg-color-for-spl(spl) and bg-color-for-delta(delta) currently return raw hex per band. If these are meant to follow the app palette, extract to a shared constants file with named tokens (SPL_HOT, SPL_LOUD, SPL_MOD, SPL_QUIET) and reuse in kiosk + spl-meter.
settings/index.tsx — clean; constants HUE_ON/HUE_WARN/HUE_DANGER at file top and only referenced downstream. Good pattern to replicate in compare (see comment above).

seed_data_creation: Attempted to seed compare with 2 scenes via localStorage.setItem('soundmap-store', {...}) but the store's ErrorBoundary caught 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading speechScore)' because seed lacked full acoustics + speech fields required by DiffRow > compare-acoustics. Recommend either (a) using the store's built-in seedDemo() action if exposed, or (b) capturing a real scene from /design → 'Guardar escena' before hitting /compare in the next iteration.

rca of the issue: DiffRow legacy hues RCA: The bulk sed pass replaced #5BA777 and #9B7EBD in inline `style={{ ... }}` blocks and in constant declarations (A_HUE, B_HUE, HUE_SYNC etc.), but missed the tailwind arbitrary-value class strings `text-[#5BA777]` / `text-[#9B7EBD]` because these are wrapped inside a `cn(better === 'b' ? ... : ...)` conditional that likely didn't match the sed regex (which probably targeted `"#5BA777"` or `#5BA777` outside brackets). Reproduction: `grep -n 'text-\[#' src/pages/compare/index.tsx` shows the two survivors on L720-721. Fix: manual replace OR extend sed pattern to `#5BA777` unconditionally (no whitespace boundary). Mitigation: reference A_HUE/B_HUE via tailwind's arbitrary syntax `text-[${A_HUE}]` — however TS template strings inside className arbitrary values don't get picked up by Tailwind's JIT scanner, so a safer fix is to use inline `style={{ color: better === 'b' ? A_HUE : B_HUE }}` on the icons instead of the className prop.
